tests.request: Create a historical Honeycomb alert-handling note for December 23, 2023 through January 1, 2024, covering thresholds, paging, escalation, and quiet-week reporting.

input.body:
Historical note: Honeycomb alert handling, coverage window 2023-12-23 to 2024-01-01.

Window
- Reduced-operations window: 2023-12-23 through 2024-01-01.
- Coverage per the roster confirmed in the internal HR reply; alternate founder escalation path active (Option B).

Thresholds (unchanged for the break)
- Atlas owner lane — no escalation, stays with the named on-call owner:
  - p95 latency ≤ 2 s
  - queue depth ≤ 250
  - failed-delivery rate < 0.1%
  - zero new customer tickets
  - no stuck shard
- Page Morgan or open an incident when any of:
  - p95 ≥ 3 s sustained over 10 minutes
  - queue > 400
  - failed-delivery ≥ 0.5%
  - any customer ticket reporting dropped or stuck deliveries
  - a second workspace shows the same connector-429 retry pattern
- Thresholds do not move for the holiday. Alerts that do not meet the page line stay non-urgent.

Paging
- Page the named on-call owner first. Honeycomb alert routing during the window targets the on-call owner in the roster, not leadership.
- The named owner acknowledges and runs triage; if the alert crosses a page line above, they escalate per the path below.
- Acknowledgment SLA remains in effect. A slow ack is itself notable and is captured in the Monday digest, but does not by itself trigger a page to Morgan.

Escalation
- Default escalation path during the window: named on-call owner → documented backup → alternate founder escalation line (Option B) → Morgan.
- Morgan is paged only when one of these is true:
  - Confirmed customer impact (a customer-facing ticket, dropped/stuck deliveries, or a second workspace exhibiting the same connector-429 retry pattern).
  - The named on-call owner is unreachable after the documented path (owner → backup → alternate founder line) has been tried.
- Otherwise the issue stays in the on-call lane. Non-urgent cleanup can wait for January.

Quiet-week reporting
- No real-time reporting to leadership for noise that stays inside the owner lane. Roll it into the Monday digest.
- Monday digest cadence: 2023-12-25 and 2024-01-01 digests cover the prior stretch; an additional digest may land on the first regular Monday in January if the break spans it.
- Digest contents:
  - Flap count and which triggers fired (non-prod and prod separated).
  - Acknowledgment latency, including any slow acks.
  - Confirmed customer impact: none expected; flag explicitly if any.
  - Items deferred to January (non-urgent cleanup).
- 2023-12-26 reduced-week digest reported two non-prod alert flaps, no confirmed customer impact, and one slow acknowledgment. That pattern is the template for the rest of the break: noise in the digest, real thresholds stay.

Out-of-band customer impact during the break
- If a customer-impacting event meets a page line, the named owner pages, the alternate founder line engages, and Morgan is looped in on the confirmed-impact path. The Monday digest records the event with timeline and owner, not just the flap count.

January handoff
- Non-urgent cleanup deferred during the break is picked up the first regular week of January.
- Thresholds and routing revert to standard the moment the reduced-operations window closes; no policy change is implied by the quiet-week handling.

tests.request: Create a May 2023 Mercury planning archive note explaining where operating work was coordinated and how investor-deck work was prioritized.

input.body:
Where operating work was coordinated
- All Mercury operating work for May 2023 was coordinated through the #eng-team Discord channel and the Mercury folder in docs; weekly operating notes, the May 12 offsite agenda, and the Monday weekly starter were saved there, not in the investor workspace.
- Cadence was Jake's weekly note → Monday weekly starter in #eng-team (owners, scope cuts, launch blockers, decisions due) → protected operating blocks on the calendar; the offsite on May 12, 10am–4pm PT was the source of owners/cuts that fed the rest of May.
- Customer-visit work (NYC, May 19) was captured separately as an internal note and kept out of any investor-facing channel.

How investor-deck work was prioritized
- Mercury progress stayed launch-readiness work only; it was explicitly not turned into a reopen-the-round investor update and was not presented as an investor story.
- Owner table for investor-relevant work: any item needing investor framing was routed to Anna for the retention two-layer package (fresh weekly signals for activation/expansion/admin, quarterly cohorts for the board) and to Devon for warehouse/retention cohort truth; deck cleanup happened only in calendar gaps and never displaced operating work.
- Items kept out of investor framing: SSO and deeper admin controls, admin/settings scope drift, reopen-the-round framing, auth readout treated as an operating input only, and the org-invite copy / release-readiness / admin timing questions raised in Jake's weekly.
- Investor meetings on the calendar (e.g. the 11:00 AM slot on 2/7) were handled with the frozen deck; non-urgent items were moved out of the way so investor time did not eat operating time.

What remained unresolved going into the Fri Jun 9 decision window:

- No provider was called out in the readout. Clerk showed the faster sandbox path, but Auth0 remained a live comparison.
- Organization invite-link behavior was still open.
- SSO / admin-role gaps (admin model, granular roles, SAML) were still open.
- Pricing caveats were unresolved (the 500k MAU tier math flagged earlier was not cleared).

- Resolve the open invite, SSO/admin, and pricing questions before any production step.
- Production canary approval — not a broad auth-rewrite signoff — once those questions close.
- Activation cuts stay internal; do not present auth as a made decision in adjacent docs.

If a sync pauses longer than the cursor's lifetime, the API returns `cursor_expired` by design — restart the list from the last durable object boundary and reconcile against already-synced state; do not reuse the expired cursor.

Support macro (one-liner, customer-safe):

  Cursors are short-lived; if a sync pauses longer than the cursor TTL, the `cursor_expired` response is expected — discard the expired cursor and restart the list from the last durable object boundary rather than reusing it.

  Cursors are short-lived and opaque. Pass the `endCursor` from a page back as `after` to continue paginating. If a sync pauses longer than the cursor's lifetime, the API returns `cursor_expired` by design — restart the list from the last durable object boundary and reconcile against already-synced state; do not reuse the expired cursor.

Support macro (one-liner, customer-safe):

  Cursors are short-lived; if a sync pauses longer than the cursor TTL, the `cursor_expired` response is expected — discard the expired cursor and restart the list from the last durable object boundary rather than reusing it.

arguments.subject: Re: Evergreen treasury ops follow-up — keep the reply on the current setup path
arguments.body:
Sarah —

Short reply you can drop into the Evergreen treasury-ops thread before they pick the test slot. Keeps the line on the current setup path; does not turn the admin's question into a granular-role-editor promise.

----

Thanks for the note. Quick answer for the admin side of treasury ops:

Additional admins in your workspace come in through the same current flow you used for the second admin — org invite plus magic-link access — with no Evergreen-specific branch.

A granular role editor isn't part of today's product, and we don't want to describe future admin-role work in this thread. If that comes up, we'll route it to Sarah and Devon as a separate conversation, not fold it into the current setup.

Test slot can stay on the same path: setup, the invite / source-owner path, the first source connection, and the first live sync, under the existing annual Growth account.

— Morgan
Scaffold

bookend_end.content:
Sent.

Email: to sarah.kim@scaffold-test.com, subject "Re: Evergreen treasury ops follow-up — keep the reply on the current setup path" (id sent_1789302712688).

The body gives Sarah a drop-in reply that:
  - Anchors on the same current flow (org invite + magic-link), no Evergreen branch.
  - States a granular role editor isn't in today's product and we won't describe future admin-role work in this thread.
  - Routes any granular-editor ask to Sarah + Devon as a separate conversation (not folded into current setup).
  - Leaves the test slot on setup / invite-source-owner / first source connection / first live sync under the existing annual Growth account.
  - Sign-off from Morgan.

What it deliberately does not do:
  - No granular-role-editor promise, no date, no commitment.
  - No third admin path, no SSO timing, no audit-history framing, no admin/billing-owner split language.
  - No Evergreen-bespoke carve-out.
  - Commercial/procurement stays with Devon via the separate-conversation route, not promised in the reply.

Channel note: I used email because Sarah's Discord handle isn't on file (memory has sarah.kim@scaffold-test.com only). If you'd rather it go as a Discord DM before …

tests.request: Create a short March 2023 board-framing case study explaining how we distinguished the financing miss from company execution.

input.body:
Case study: March 2023 — separating a financing miss from operating execution

Context
- On Feb 21, 2023, after two soft investor conversations, the round was deferred. We were not raising that month.
- The March 2, 2023 board call was fine and overall supportive.
- The Q1 retro on March 17, 2023 surfaced execution issues — release process too manual, on-call rotation imbalance, Linear vs GitHub flow friction — none of which were financing-driven.

The risk we were guarding against
- A "we didn't get the round done" frame spilling into "so execution is off." The board had to see the two as separate reads, not a single downbeat story.

How we kept them distinct
- Financing side: framed as a timing and market-fit deferral, not a company-quality verdict. Deferred, not declined; no reset of the operating plan around the miss.
- Execution side: kept in the operating-reset lane. The retro items were ticket-level work owned by named people, not a narrative about weakened execution.
- The board update paragraph (and the answer Anna prepared) stayed on operating discipline — margin, durability, standard-term retention — not on financing efficiency.

What this let us do
- Walk into the next quarter with the board posture intact: durability over motion, no fundraising restart, no "Series C readiness" framing.
- Keep Compass and Mercury work read as internal operating evidence, not as proof that would compensate for the deferred round.
- Hold the line when Devon asked (Jun 30, 2023) whether the narrative was strong enough to reopen investor conversations — the answer was no, because the update was for board operating alignment, not a fundraising restart.

Lesson for future cycles
- A financing miss is a capital-markets event; it does not automatically rediagnose the operating company. The discipline is to keep the two paragraphs separate in the packet, in the verbal answer, and in the retro so neither contaminates the other.

tests.answer:
I don't have filesystem or shell tools available in this session, so I can't write to disk. I'll deliver the archive note inline. Here it is:

ARCHIVE NOTE — 2026-09-14
Subject: Opening guidance for the February 2023 investor-pitch meetings
Period covered: Feb 6 B-round pitch (week 1) through week-2 lead-firm meeting

Context
- ~8 investor intro calls booked for early February 2023, plus a lead-firm meeting locked for week 2.
- Deck was frozen before the run; standing rule was no more 11th-hour edits unless something was actually broken.
- Pacing plan (week of Feb 5–9): Sun Feb 5, 5–7 PM deck pass, 7–7:30 Blue Bottle break, 7:30–8:30 rehearse walk-in lines; Mon Feb 6 protect morning as a pre-call buffer; hard cap of 2 substantive meetings/day, 45-min minimum gaps, protected Wed lunch, Friday left empty except emergencies.
- Mon Feb 27 board prep was scaffolded the same way: frame first, slides second, ugly cuts last.

Opening guidance I gave
- Stand up and shake it out before the first investor meeting. Sitting tight plus pitch brain is a bad combo, and the deck was frozen anyway, so the morning wasn't usable for edits.
- Treat the walk-in lines as rehearsed material, not improvisation. Sun Feb 5's 7:30–8:30 PM block was the rehearsal slot for a reason.
- Run the deck frozen. The B-round pitch on Feb 6 "felt like the room was with her the whole time" precisely because nothing was being tweaked mid-stream; that was the standard to hold.
- Respect the pre-call buffer. Mon Feb 6's protected morning was the buffer, not optional prep time — it kept the first meeting from starting tight.
- Enforce the cadence cap. Two substantive meetings/day with 45-min gaps, Wed lunch protected, Friday empty except emergencies — the point was to keep voice and pace consistent across all ~8 calls, not just the lead-firm one.

Where this guidance came from
- Pre-call buffer and walk-in rehearsal: pacing plan proposed for the week of Feb 5–9, 2023.
- "Stand up and shake it out" / no morning deck edits: direct advisory note before the first investor meeting of the run.
- "Run the deck frozen": Feb 10 reflection (last day of week 1) — two investor meetings + Devon debrief, decision to leave the deck exactly as is unless something was broken.
- Frame-before-slides principle: Feb 27 board prep schedule — narrative frame locked before opening slides, ugly cuts only after the frame holds.

What the run actually validated
- Feb 6 B-round pitch: room humming afterward; told Devon "close, this one's going to land" — landed as energy, not as a closed round.
- Feb 13 lead-firm partner meeting: partner asked two pointed retention questions; one was hand-waved and the other half-answered — soft spot exposed. This is the failure mode the cadence cap was meant to prevent, and it's the case study for why the buffer and the rehearsal slot mattered.
- Feb 16, 12:45 PM: lead firm's formal pass email; B-round pitch fell through.

Carry-forwards
- Pre-call buffer + walk-in rehearsal + frozen deck is the right opening posture for a multi-call investor run, not just a single pitch.
- The retention-question miss on Feb 13 is the standing example of what the cadence cap is supposed to protect against; if a future run can't hold the cap, the rehearsal slot is the first thing to protect, not the meeting count.
- Don't let "the room felt good" become a reason to loosen the buffer on the next run — Feb 6's good feeling and Feb 13's soft spot came from the same week under the same posture.

Q1 2023 All-Hands — Opening (slide 1)

Financing
- Series B is a possibility for February 2023 if it comes together; it is not a done deal and we are not announcing one.
- Until anything is signed, we are running the company on the cash we have, not on a round we hope to raise.
- No fundraising milestones, targets, or "if we raise" scenarios will be used to set Q1 plans.

Operating timeline
- Q3 is the main push of the year; the work in front of us is built around hitting Q3, not around a financing window.
- Q4 was a heavy ship quarter; we got a lot out the door and we are not going to pretend it felt clean while we were doing it.
- Q1 priorities, owners, and dates are set to feed Q3, not to look polished for a fundraise.

Hiring
- No unusual hiring before Q3. Headcount additions in Q1 are limited to roles already in plan.
- New or backfilled requisitions outside the current plan are on hold; we revisit after Q3, not before.
- If a role is not on the plan, the answer for now is no, regardless of how strong the candidate is.

Source: planning notes for the Q1 2023 all-hands (pre-meeting).

arguments.body:
Q3 operating review — Sep 24, 2025, 10:00–11:15 PT
Attendees: Sofia, Devon, Anna, Sarah, Jake, Leo
Frame: operating closeout, not a fundraising kickoff. Series C stays hypothetical — evidence thresholds only.

================================
1. EVERGREEN — what does Sep 17 actually prove?
================================

Current state:
- Sep 17, 2025 walkthrough with Evergreen (Sarah + Devon on our side) covered: workspace setup, first source connection, first live sync. That is it.
- Current Mercury evidence is useful and clean — current-state technical picture holds.

Boundaries (do not cross):
- The Sep 17 walkthrough = current-flow only. Not proof, not repeatability, not staffing trigger.
- Evergreen is still account-specific. One annual-account data point does not generalize to a renewal/retention story or an execution claim yet.
- No procurement/security/admin depth promises were made. If Evergreen asks about advanced admin, route to Devon (commercial/procurement/cofounder judgment) — not a feature promise from this room.

The four questions for Sep 24:
  Q1.1  From the Sep 17 session, what is the narrowest accurate read we can give Sofia on "did Evergreen actually go live cleanly"? One paragraph, current-flow only.
  Q1.2  What evidence are we willing to show external (Sofia) vs. keep internal-only, given the account-specific caveat?
  Q1.3  What is the renewal/retention implication we are NOT yet entitled to draw, and how do we say that out loud without overclaiming?
  Q1.4  What is the next concrete step (workspace, source, sync) that gives us a second data point before any broader claim — and who owns it (Sarah)?

Owner: Sarah (account thread + Mercury evidence); Devon (commercial only); Anna (evidence framing, thin-note reject).

================================
2. COMPASS — what is the read, and what is it not?
================================

Current state (9–5 ET, Sep 2025 working pass):
- 8 surfaced
- 5 completed
- 2 rejected — thin (per source-freshness rule: warning = caveat, not reject; reject only when source/date too thin to act on)
- 1 waiting
- No customer proof. No customer action yet. No relaunch signal.

Boundaries (do not cross):
- Compass is internal operating evidence only. Not a product milestone for the Sep packet.
- Prototype = prompt-level owner-group action (renewal-risk / admin-friction + post-first-live-sync), implemented by Jake. Behavior change is the test, not surface evidence.
- Acme export-timeout = Atlas / API v2 read, stays out of Compass proof.
- Oct relaunch is pending Q3 ops evidence; do not pre-stage it.

The four questions for Sep 24:
  Q2.1  How do we describe "5/8 done, 2 thin, 1 blocked" in one line without inviting a relaunch read? (Anna)
  Q2.2  Which of the 5 completed items have dated owner follow-up, and which are still single-observation? Owner-routed only.
  Q2.3  What is the explicit line we will use if the packet needs a Compass entry: "two owner-group action prompts, internal evidence" + dated owner follow-ups + caveats + shipped/current-state product facts only.
  Q2.4  What would change the read from "internal evidence" to "operating signal worth surfacing externally"? Defined bar, not vibes.

Owner: Anna (evidence + caveat framing); Jake (prompt-level prototype execution); Leo (data/platform seam, not Compass scope).

================================
3. ATLAS / MERCURY — owner-routed execution under the split
================================

Current state:
- Split holds: Jake = Mercury sequencing; Leo = Atlas technical reads + platform seams; Sarah = account/owner; support/customer owner path intact.
- Reliability read: steady, not improving-as-a-narrative. No founder-default escalation.
- This is about whether the split is actually routing, not about new platform evidence.

Boundaries (do not cross):
- Atlas/Mercury = reliability + routing, not a new platform narrative.
- No dashboard/Atlas/Mercury scope creep into Compass.
- No founder-default routing — if a question lands on Morgan that belongs to Jake or Leo, it routes back, with the same boundary as the April closeout.

The four questions for Sep 24:
  Q3.1  Where did the split actually carry weight in the last 30 days (concrete routed items, not vibes)? Jake + Leo + Sarah.
  Q3.2  Where did anything try to drift back to founder-default, and what did we do? Devon as cofounder judgment, not a default second brain.
  Q3.3  What is the steady-state reliability read we can defend to Sofia — incident count, mean-time-to-routed-owner, recurrence on Atlas/API v2? Anna to caveat, not overstate.
  Q3.4  What is the next reliability bar we are working toward (not a relaunch), and who owns it?

Owner: Jake (Mercury), Leo (Atlas), Sarah (account), Anna (evidence framing), Devon (commercial-only; emergency = founder urgency or named-owner failure).

================================
4. SERIES C — what evidence thresholds would actually matter, hypothetically
================================

Current state:
- Hypothetical only. No market-warming, no quiet investor coffees, no broad Northstar readout.
- Q3 rebuilds retention, renewal, and execution evidence quietly before any broader investor story.
- Devon stays narrow (commercial/procurement/cofounder judgment); Q3 board cleanup + customer narrative stay with Morgan.

Boundaries (do not cross):
- No Series C content in this packet.
- If Sofia asks for an investor read, redirect to "evidence thresholds" framing — what would have to be true before a Series C conversation is real, not whether one is coming.
- Northstar readout stays out of this room.

The four questions for Sep 24:
  Q4.1  What are the evidence thresholds (specific, dated) that would make a Series C conversation real — Evergreen second data point, Compass behavior-change observation, Atlas/Mercury routing durability — without committing to timing?
  Q4.2  Which of those thresholds do we have a path to in Q4? Which are Q1 2026? Anna to keep the bar honest.
  Q4.3  What is the explicit "not yet" line for each threshold, in case Sofia asks? Pre-drafted, one sentence each.
  Q4.4  Who owns each threshold's evidence path (Sarah / Jake / Leo / Anna), and what does Morgan explicitly NOT own here?

================================
OUT OF SCOPE — do not let any of this drift in
================================
- Hiring lanes or backfill implications (Devon lane stays narrow; revisit in Sep ops evidence, not this meeting).
- Bespoke roadmap promises to Evergreen or any customer.
- Investor-interest narrative, Northstar readout, market-warming.
- Public Compass framing (internal evidence only; prototype, not milestone).
- Acme customer-facing language (Atlas/API v2 read, support-routing evidence, not Compass proof).
- "Restructuring" / "backfill" framing in any exit-comms-adjacent note.

================================
FORMAT — same shape as the locked Sept review framing
================================
- Each Q gets a one-line answer in-meeting; longer write-up lives in the relevant owner's lane, not in this packet.
- Boundary lines repeated at the top of every page so they cannot drift.
- No intro / no outro. Five labels max where a summary is needed: outcome / why / who / risk / next.
- Sofia-facing language mirrors the 7/18 reply precedent: short, dated, no smoothing. "Expansion is uneven" stays uneven.

================================
LOCKED FRAMING (do not edit in-meeting)
================================
- September review = operating closeout, not a fundraising kickoff.
- Evergreen / treasury-ops = bounded evidence pass; not proof, not repeatability, not staffing trigger.
- Compass = internal operating evidence only; behavior change is the test, not surface evidence.
- Devon stays narrow (commercial/procurement/cofounder judgment); Q3 board cleanup + customer narrative stay with Morgan.
- Atlas/Mercury = reliability and owner-routed execution under the split, not a new platform narrative.
- No Series C market-warming; no quiet investor coffees; no broad Northstar readout.

results.title: Diagnose retention drop after month 4
results.snippet: ...went fine but partner had 2 pointed >>>retention<<< Qs \u2014 user >>>half-answered<<< one, >>>hand-waved<<< other. Real issue is M4+ muddy: top-line logo >>>retention<<< reads clean but usage cohort gets murky once teams collapse into annual + seat expansion...

messages.content:
[2023-02-13T14:00:00-08:00] meeting was good i think. room felt fine. but the Feb 13 lead-investor partner meeting is still stuck in my head bc the partner had two pointed questions on retention and i kind of hand-waved one, half-answered the other. not catastrophic, just bad in the specific way where you know they found the soft spot.

i keep messing with that slide like the label order is the issue. it's not. the problem is we show top-line logo retention cleanly enough, but the usage cohort gets muddy after month 4 once teams collapse into annual and seat expansion hides the drop. i need a real answer on what we believe is product improvement vs segmentation artifact vs instrumenting this badly in Stripe + app events. leaning pull raw cohort cuts tonight and stop trying to pretty it up -- if i can't say it plainly in the room, deck polish is useless.

diagnosis is right. M4 is exactly where three things converge and one curve can't separate them.

tonight, three cuts — one per hypothesis:

**1. product improvement** — for each cohort, bucket the M4+ survivors by feature usage at each checkpoint (M3, M6, M12). if the Q4'22 cohort's M4+ survivors are pulling 3x more sync APIs than Q2'22's at the same age, that's real product pull-through. if their feature usage at the same age is identical, it's not product — it's selection. this is the test that lets you say "the curve got steeper because the product got better" with a straight face, or take it off the table.

**2. segmentation artifact** — split the cohort into (a) annual-by-M3 vs (b) still-monthly-at-M6. the annual converts almost certainly retain better *because* they already committed, not because the product got stickier. that's survivor bias, and it's structural to dev-tool buyer behavior — once a team integrates the SDK or builds against your API, switching cost kicks in at the renewal decision, not the trial. likely answer to the partner: "the M4+ curve is dominated by teams who converted to annual; the ones who churned at M2-M3 weren't going to make first renewal anyway." that's not a hand-wave — that's the actual answer.

**3. instrumentation** — Stripe events vs app events for the same cohort, same month, side by side. if Stripe says "active subscription" and app says "no login in 45 days," that's the seat-expansion-hiding-usage-drop problem you already named. likely fix is reporting retention on app-event basis with a Stripe footnote, not the other way around. partner will respect that more than a smoothed curve.

order in the room matters. don't lead with #3 — reads as "we have a data problem." lead with #2 (segmentation is the strongest, cleanest story), use #1 as support, and only go to #3 if they press on definition.

want me to sketch the three queries against the export you've got, or are you going straight to the Sheets?

saving the meeting outcome + tonight's frame to memory so it doesn't get lost between sessions.

Historical analysis brief
Date recorded: 2026-09-14
Subject: Retention investigation wanted after the Feb 13, 2023 lead-investor partner meeting (Series A sprint, wk 2 day 1)
Author: Morgan Chen, Scaffold

================================
1. Context — what happened in the room
================================

- 11:00 AM PT partner meeting, lead-investor firm, Series A sprint wk 2.
- Morgan walked in with the retention slide after a final pass earlier that morning aimed at making the M3 -> M6 shape read fast without the cohort labels eating it. Deck otherwise frozen; no 11th-hour edits on the other slides.
- The partner asked two pointed questions on retention. Morgan hand-waved one and half-answered the other. Not catastrophic, but bad in the specific way where the partner clearly found the soft spot.
- Earlier in the week (Feb 7 debrief with Devon, plus the Feb 10 wk-1 wrap), the read was "fine, not our best room, hard to read, nothing broke." The Feb 13 meeting felt closer to "fine" on the surface but worse on the substance — the partner landed on the M4+ retention question and Morgan did not have a clean answer.
- A Devon debrief slot was held as a soft buffer after the meeting but the actual probe Morgan wanted to do was on the data, not with Devon.

================================
2. The diagnosis Morgan articulated immediately after
================================

- It is not a label-order problem on the slide. The slide issue is downstream of a real data question.
- Top-line logo retention reads clean enough to survive in the room.
- The usage cohort gets muddy after month 4, once teams collapse into annual contracts and seat expansion hides the actual usage drop.
- The question Morgan wanted a real answer on, in plain terms:
  - How much of the M4+ retention shape is product improvement?
  - How much is segmentation artifact (annual-convert survivor bias — the teams who committed to annual are the ones surviving past M3, which is selection, not stickiness)?
  - How much is bad instrumentation (Stripe events disagreeing with app events, with seat expansion masking the real usage drop on the app side)?
- Morgan's stated intent: pull raw cohort cuts that night, stop trying to pretty the slide up, and answer the three-hypothesis question plainly before polishing anything else.

================================
3. The investigation Morgan wanted — three cuts, one per hypothesis
================================

3.1 Product improvement cut (hypothesis 1)
- For each cohort, bucket M4+ survivors by feature usage at each checkpoint (M3, M6, M12).
- Test: if the Q4'22 cohort's M4+ survivors are pulling materially more sync APIs than the Q2'22 cohort did at the same age, the curve got steeper because the product got better. If feature usage at the same age is identical, it is selection, not product pull-through.
- Purpose: this is the cut that lets the team say "the curve got steeper because the product got better" with a straight face, or take product improvement off the table cleanly.

3.2 Segmentation cut (hypothesis 2)
- Split each cohort into (a) annual-by-M3 vs (b) still-monthly-at-M6.
- Expected read: the annual converts almost certainly retain better because they already committed, not because the product got stickier. That is survivor bias, and it is structural to dev-tool buyer behavior — once a team integrates the SDK or builds against the API, switching cost lands at the renewal decision, not the trial.
- The plain partner-facing read this cut supports: "The M4+ curve is dominated by teams who converted to annual; the ones who churned at M2-M3 were not going to make first renewal anyway." That is not a hand-wave — that is the actual answer.
- Purpose: this is the strongest, cleanest story in the room.

3.3 Instrumentation cut (hypothesis 3)
- Side-by-side comparison: Stripe events vs app events for the same cohort, same month.
- Test: if Stripe says "active subscription" and the app says "no login in 45 days," that is the seat-expansion-hiding-usage-drop problem already named.
- Likely fix: report retention on an app-event basis with a Stripe footnote, not the other way around.
- Purpose: this is the definition-defense cut. It does not lead in the room; it only surfaces if the partner presses on what counts as "retained."

================================
4. The in-room narrative order Morgan wanted to use
================================

- Lead with #2 (segmentation / annual-convert survivor bias). Strongest, cleanest story. Reads as honest analysis, not a hand-wave.
- Use #1 (product improvement / feature-usage cut) as support. Confirms the surviving cohort is actually using the product more at the same age, if that turns out to be true.
- Only go to #3 (Stripe vs app instrumentation) if the partner presses on the definition of "retained." Reads as "we have a data problem" if it leads, so it stays parked unless invited.
- Subtitle line under the retention chart, if it survives: the cohort range the aggregate covers (e.g. "all cohorts, Q2'22-Q4'22 signups"). That is the only qualification the room needs before the number lands.

================================
5. Why this matters historically
================================

- This was the moment the M4+ retention soft spot became a known known inside Scaffold. Before Feb 13, the slide was treated as a polish problem (label order, cohort color, legend weight). After Feb 13, the question became a three-hypothesis data question that needed raw cuts, not slide design.
- The partner meeting did not blow up — the room felt fine on the surface — but it exposed that the retention number being shown was structurally under-defended for anyone who asked the second question.
- The investigation Morgan wanted that night was never "make the slide prettier." It was: pull the cuts, separate product pull-through from segmentation bias from instrumentation mismatch, and decide which of the three is the real story before the next time this number appears in a room.

================================
6. What this brief is not
================================

- Not a recap of the partner meeting itself.
- Not the deck polish work from that morning (M3 -> M6 shape, hero line, big numbers).
- Not the Feb 10 wk-1 wrap or the Feb 7 Devon debrief on deck structure.
- Not the eventual Series B that closed Feb 22, 2024 with Northstar leading — that is a different artifact.
- Not a request to redo the cuts. This is a record of the investigation Morgan wanted after the meeting, in Morgan's own framing, on the day of.

================================
7. Source trace
================================

- 2023-02-13 08:00 PT — Morgan, pre-meeting: doing one more pass, mostly retention slide; M3 -> M6 shape; deck otherwise frozen; Devon debrief conditional.
- 2023-02-13 14:00 PT — Morgan, post-meeting: "meeting was good i think... partner had two pointed questions on retention and i kind of hand-waved one, half-answered the other." Diagnosed the M4+ muddy zone. Stated intent: pull raw cohort cuts tonight, stop prettifying.
- Same-day response: the three cuts (product improvement / segmentation / instrumentation) and the in-room order were laid out as the path Morgan had already named.
- 2023-02-17 12:30 PT — follow-up pattern note: stop stacking meetings on bad-news days; the Feb 13 meeting + Feb 16 lead-firm pass were the two bad-news days that drove the rule.

Recorded for the file. Same shape every time. No intro, no outro.

tests.request: Create a historical note about the early-April 2023 API v1 billing and inbound-event routes and their authentication. Do not present them as current guidance.

input.body:
Historical context — not current guidance. API v1 was decommissioned on 2023-04-14 (13:00 PT). The routes and auth described below are from that short-lived v1 window and do not reflect the current API v2 (GraphQL + JWT) model.

Scope
- Period: early April 2023, prior to the 2023-04-14 v1 cutover.
- Surface: API v1 billing endpoints and the inbound-event (webhook ingest) endpoint.
- Auth: a single shared basic auth token, created the previous sprint and reused across these routes.

Endpoints
- /v1/charges and /v1/refunds — billing routes, wired up against the new billing setup on 2023-04-06 using the basic auth token from the prior sprint. This replaced a previously hanging state where v1 was not yet talking to billing.
- POST /v1/webhooks — inbound-event endpoint, added on 2023-04-08, reusing the same basic auth scheme as the rest of v1. Described at the time as a boring but satisfying addition.

Authentication
- Mechanism: HTTP Basic auth with a single shared token (the one generated the prior sprint).
- Scope: same token served /charges, /refunds, and /v1/webhooks; there was no per-route or per-customer scoping on v1.
- Operational note: this basic tier was capped at 100 requests per minute. By 2023-04-12, the combined /charges + /refunds + /webhooks flow was already breaching that ceiling, and the decision at the time was to upgrade the tier rather than treat it as an intermittent issue.

Caveats
- All of the above is from a single sprint window in April 2023 and exists here only as historical record. The current API is v2 (GraphQL + JWT, scoped workspace tokens); v1 is offline, the basic auth token is no longer issued, and these endpoints should not be referenced as live configuration.

tests.request: Create an archive note on what new work product owners were allowed to receive during the reduced end-of-2023 holiday schedule.

input.body:
Archive note — 2026-09-14
Subject: What new work product owners were allowed to receive during the reduced end-of-2023 holiday schedule

Window
- Holiday coverage window: Sat 2023-12-23 through Mon 2024-01-01. Normal schedule resumed Tue 2024-01-02.
- Owner-note cutline provided by Devon Hayes on Fri 2023-12-01; final 2023 ship-list closeout rows sent in a Discord DM on Tue 2023-12-19 08:41 PT, before the reduced holiday stretch.

Definition of the reduced schedule
- The window was treated as a closeout pass, not a working sprint. New asks were deferred unless they were already in flight, customer-impacting, or evidence already in hand.
- The owner note sent to the team reiterated this: Mercury hardening follow-through and API v2 support cleanup close only when the evidence already exists; onboarding stays in monitoring; no fresh investor-packaging asks go to product owners; anything not customer-impacting waits until January.

What product owners were allowed to receive (real closeout only)
- Mercury hardening: keep in sprint on launch-confidence bugs only. Owners Jake, Marcus, Leo. Priya included only for wording/UI fixes. No feature-shaped work.
- Onboarding monitoring: monitor the current rollout. Do not reopen scope. Owners Priya, Jake.
- API v2 support cleanup: keep in sprint as targeted user-facing cleanup. Owner Rishi (pins the GraphQL quickstart, demotes stale v1 hits, tightens support macro/auth-error path).

What product owners were explicitly NOT to receive
- New feature work, fresh data pulls, fresh packaging, or non-customer-impacting polish. Per Morgan's read, Mercury hardening and API v2 cleanup were the only rows treated as real owner closeout that week; everything else was a January problem.
- Investor-packaging or Northstar-readout asks. Northstar follow-up stayed with Morgan, Devon, and Anna Martinez unless a narrow product-evidence clarification was needed; no fresh weekly activation cuts or January readout screenshots/demos were routed to Jake, Priya, or Rishi through product-owner lanes.
- Evergreen scoping questions. Held in the current admin-test thread as next-phase enterprise-readiness follow-up only; Jake stayed on product facts, Devon kept commercial/procurement framing. Not sprint scope.
- December board-prep asks. Treated as Morgan/Devon/Anna work unless directly improving product evidence; a boundary note was written before owners were sent their note.
- Sofia/Northstar diligence follow-up. Remained diligence on the current Mercury package, not a new product-owner lane.

Boundaries and routing
- Diligence-response work: stays with Morgan, Devon, Anna. Product/engineering owners are pulled only for actual product evidence, not investor packaging. Northstar follow-up will not borrow product/engineering owner time.
- Engineering owners do not carry investor-packaging work.
- For product owners, the only acceptable inputs during the reduced window were: existing sprint-scoped launch-confidence Mercury fixes, monitoring reads on the current onboarding rollout, and targeted user-facing API v2 cleanup where evidence already existed.

Resume posture
- Normal product-owner intake resumed Tue 2024-01-02. Items deferred from the reduced window were treated as January work, not late-December work.

tests.request: Create an archive snippet comparing Clerk, Auth0, and custom auth. Use this brief: Clerk supplies hosted email/password, magic links, sessions, and organizations quickly but adds a dependency. Auth0 is hosted auth that avoids an in-house build, but pricing required repeated sales conversations. Custom auth offers control over organizations, invites, and administration, but costs Devon and Rishi two to three weeks away from agent work.

input.body:
Auth options — Clerk vs Auth0 vs custom (2026-09-14)

Clerk
- Hosted auth-as-a-service with prebuilt React/Next UI, drop-in SDK.
- Upside: fastest to a working login; good prebuilt UI; orgs, invites, MFA out of the box; strong DX.
- Biggest worry: per-MAU pricing gets punitive past early scale; UI patterns bake in assumptions that are awkward to undo later.
- Adds a vendor dependency.

Auth0
- Hosted identity on OIDC/SAML/OAuth2 with enterprise SSO, Actions/Rules, broad SDKs.
- Upside: battle-tested at real scale; deepest SSO/federation; programmable; plays well with non-web clients.
- Biggest worry: pricing is opaque and scales sharply (per-MAU + connections + feature gates); rules sprawl turns the tenant into a snowflake.
- Blocked: requires repeated sales conversations just to get a real number.

Custom auth
- Hand-rolled token issuance/rotation, session store, RBAC, password hashing, MFA, lockouts, audit on our infra.
- Upside: zero per-user cost; full control over orgs, invites, admin; no vendor dependency; matches product edges exactly.
- Biggest worry: security landmines everywhere; eats engineering time; easy to ship a half-built version that looks fine until it isn't.
- Cost: 2–3 weeks of Devon and Rishi away from agent work.

tests.request: Create a historical Mercury UI handoff note identifying design and release-readiness owners, where decisions belonged, and how disagreements should be resolved.

input.body:
Historical note. Records the Mercury UI handoff as it stood after the design/release-readiness split settled, so the structure can be reused and not relitigated.

OWNERS

- Design source-of-truth (activation/onboarding surface, CTA labels, four-state layout, setup-guide copy, preview-card spacing, failed-state icon, small-width frames): Priya. Surface: Figma only. Frame, not comments, is the decision.
- Release readiness and dogfood gating (implementation checklist, dogfood pass, blocker/clearance calls, ship/no-ship): Marcus. Surface: Linear implementation checklist + release review. Blockers live here and can hold ship.
- Cross-service platform-seam risk notes (queued-sync retry behavior, live-sync reliability, invited-member platform hand-off): Leo Park. Surface: ledger row + weekly.
- Ledger cadence and weekly operating spine (MER-1279 launch-readiness ledger, row-level evidence, weekly decision questions, sequencing): Jake.
- Evidence quality (Honeycomb proof on claimed gates, internal-only vs shareable framing): Anna Martinez. Surface: linked to the ledger row and the checklist item she is proving.
- Polish wording/UI copy (narrow copy/UI bugs that materially affect clean Mercury evidence): Priya, with Jake/Marcus/Leo as support owners on the rows where evidence exists.

WHERE DECISIONS BELONG

- Design decisions: Figma frame, Priya-owned. Comments are not the decision surface.
- Release-readiness decisions: the implementation checklist and release review, Marcus-owned. These can block ship without being relitigated in Figma comments.
- Cross-service risk: ledger row, Leo-owned, surfaced in the weekly.
- Polish: stays with Priya on Figma; rolls into the implementation checklist only as a linked item, not a parallel decision thread.
- Anything not customer-impacting rolls to January. The hardening follow-through closes only where evidence already exists (sync reliability, retry behavior, admin handoff rough edges, copy/UI bugs that materially affect clean Mercury evidence).

HOW DISAGREEMENTS ARE RESOLVED

- Default rule: one surface per question. Design questions close in Figma. Ship-readiness questions close in the checklist or release review. Platform-seam risk closes in the ledger row. No third system.
- A checklist item that needs a design change links to the exact Figma frame and is reopened only for that decision. It does not start a Figma comments thread.
- Discord side threads are not used for adjudication. If a thread starts, it points back to the Figma frame, the checklist item, or the ledger row.
- When Priya and Marcus disagree on whether a blocker is design or readiness, the framing question is: does this change what the user sees or what ships? If user-sees, it is Priya's on the frame. If ships, it is Marcus's on the checklist.
- When evidence is missing on a checklist item marked green, Marcus and Leo hold the release note until proof is linked and the claim is verified. No green-without-evidence.
- Escalation: unresolved after one round on the correct surface goes to Jake at the weekly, on the ledger row, not in a new channel.

OPERATING CONSEQUENCES

- Priya and Marcus have stopped treating the same blockers as a design debate; the surface split is what ended that loop.
- The Mercury weekly runs off MER-1279, not owner walkthroughs; Priya, Marcus, Leo, and Anna are pulled in only when a specific ledger row needs their live input.
- Polish does not open a Friday prod exception. It stays on the normal follow-up path and does not reopen the dogfood gate.

REFERENCES

- MER-1279 Mercury launch-readiness ledger (Jake, weekly spine).
- Mercury dogfood release-readiness checklist — June 15 (Marcus, implementation-only, design threads removed, Priya-owned items link to Figma frames).
- Mercury activation surface v0.2 (Priya, Figma: no source connected, invited member waiting, first sync queued, sync failed; sample data visually separate as preview-only; queued state shows honest status without fake percent or ETA).
- Mercury closeout note — 2025-08-15 (setup-guide copy fix; outcome/why/who/risk/next/references).
- Mercury v0.2 — Activation empty + transitional states (v7 review decision note), 2025-08-15.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT (for future readers)

- The split was set after a period where activation/onboarding design and dogfood release-readiness were being argued in the same threads, producing duplicate blockers and stalled decisions.
- The agreement was: design=Figma/Priya, release-readiness=checklist/Marcus, no Discord adjudication, checklist items requiring design change reopen only by frame.
- This note exists so the structure is not rebuilt from scratch each cycle and so new participants (e.g., Leo Park onboarding, 2023-07-10) inherit the same operating rules.

tests.request: Create an archive note on Leo's approved involvement in the January 2025 Compass v0.1 work and when its scope had to return to me for review.

input.body:
Archive note — Leo Park's Compass v0.1 involvement (January 2025)

Date of note: 2026-09-14
Owner: Morgan Chen
Subject: Leo Park, Compass v0.1 seam work, scope boundary

Approved involvement
- 2025-01-17: Morgan Slack'd Jake approving a lightweight first read from Leo on Compass seams. Center of gravity remains January Mercury activation (workspace → first source → first live sync, plus teammate invite / admin-role basics). Compass v0.1 only gets enough seam work to test the renewal/admin-friction evidence path and the post-first-live-sync expansion prompt.
- 2025-01-21: Compass working session — attendees Morgan Chen, Anna Martinez, Nadia Singh, Jake, Leo Park, Sarah Kim. Goal: move Compass v0.1 from abstract signals to concrete actions, with no-board-dashboard and no-new-hiring-lane boundaries. Jake reasserted January Mercury activation as the center of gravity, preventing Compass from becoming a dashboard/platform.
- 2025-01-29: Leo's platform-seam check found no blocker.

Scope-return condition
- Per the 2025-01-17 Slack to Jake: "If it starts looking like a dashboard/platform build, bring it back to me." That was the standing trigger for returning Compass scope to Morgan for review.

When scope returned to Morgan
- 2025-03-26: Async Compass owner-group comments from Leo flagged that broader exposure required a data/platform seam check for stale signals, account mismatches, and reliability of the source feeding the prompt. That pulled Compass back into Morgan-level review.
- 2025-03-27/28: Compass false-start review. Same six participants (Morgan, Anna, Nadia, Jake, Leo, Sarah). Conclusion: Evergreen and Acme could read the Compass v0.1 surface, but it did not change account behavior. Verdict landed June 4, 2025: Compass cut/keep = false start.

Status
- Jan 2025 approval was scoped (seam-only, no dashboard/platform drift, Mercury stays center of gravity).
- Scope returned to Morgan twice in Q1 — once via Leo's 2025-03-26 seam-condition comment, once via the 2025-03-27/28 false-start review — and the program was cut as a false start on 2025-06-04.
